name: Kitzbühel

seo.title: Kitzbühel ski resort guide
seo.description: KitzSki links seven municipalities with 233 km of pistes and 57 lifts between 800 and 2,000 metres, and the Hahnenkamm downhill runs every January.
seo.twitterDescription: 233 km of pistes, 57 lifts, 800-2,000 m, and the Streif above the medieval town.
seo.webpageDescription: Ski facts, season dates, where to stay and how to get to Kitzbühel in Tyrol, Austria.

h1: Kitzbühel ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Kitzbühel is a medieval walled town with a World Cup downhill above it. KitzSki links seven municipalities across Tyrol and Salzburg with 233 kilometres of piste between 800 and 2,000 metres, ski racing has been held here since 1895, and the 2026/27 season runs from 6 November 2026 to 4 April 2027.
stayOverview: Kitzbühel splits into a historic town and a ski area far larger than it. Staying inside the walls puts restaurants and both valley lifts within walking distance; the Hahnenkamm side gets you onto the part of the mountain that opens first; Kirchberg is on the same pass for less; and Jochberg and Pass Thurn sit high enough to open in early November.
hotelIntro: Book against the season you intend to ski. The core Hahnenkamm-Fleckalm area opens in late November, but the full lift connection across to Resterhöhe only runs from 11 December 2026 to 29 March 2027.
rentalCars: A car helps if you want to move between Kitzbühel, Kirchberg and Pass Thurn, and KitzSki publishes live capacity for the car parks at each valley station. Kitzbühel also has a railway station on the Salzburg-Innsbruck line.

airports.name: Munich, Innsbruck or Salzburg
airports.text: KitzSki names Munich, Innsbruck and Salzburg as the airports for Kitzbühel. The resort does not publish transfer times, so check the route for the airport you choose.

travelTips.title: Free for beginners
travelTips.text: Every village in the ski area has a practice lift in the valley that is free of charge - ten in all.

travelTips.title: When it opens
travelTips.text: Resterkogel opens 6 November 2026, the Hahnenkamm core area in late November, and the full connection from 11 December 2026 to 29 March 2027.

travelTips.title: Groomed or not
travelTips.text: Of the 233 piste kilometres, 196 are groomed; a further 41 km is marked as ski route and left ungroomed.
travelTips.sourceLabel: Kitzbueheler Alpen: KitzSki facts (data provision by KitzSki)

travelTips.title: Parking
travelTips.text: KitzSki shows live capacity for the car parks at each valley station, and the Fleckalmbahn, Pengelstein, Maierl and Gaisberg car parks are free.

highlights.title: The Streif
highlights.text: The Hahnenkamm downhill course, raced every January since ski racing started here in 1895, is open to the public as a marked piste outside race week.

highlights.title: Hahnenkammbahn
highlights.text: The cable car from Hahnenkammstrasse in the town centre serves the core ski area, which opens first each season.

highlights.title: Kitzbüheler Horn
highlights.text: The second mountain above the town, reaching 1,996 metres, with skiing from 28 November 2026 to 21 March 2027.

highlights.title: Gaisberg toboggan run
highlights.text: A toboggan run on the Gaisberg reached by its own chairlift from Kirchberg.
highlights.sourceLabel: Kitzbueheler Alpen: KitzSki facts (data provision by KitzSki)

highlights.title: 3S cable car to Jochberg
highlights.text: The 3S links Pengelstein across the valley to Jochberg and Resterhöhe, the high end of the ski area.

highlights.title: Free valley lifts
highlights.text: Ten practice lifts in the valley, one in each village of the ski area, are free to use.
